title: Lane lint on a stacked PR flags a head that does not hold its base branch's current head
why: A stacked PR can pass lane lint while it conflicts with its base's live head, because the lint reads the head against the base and never checks that the head holds the base's head. The conflict surfaces only at batch release.
note: Incident (lane bg-tail-loses-verdict, session_013NEJL3ZjZdzrS8tBezxY85, 02:20 CST Nov 9): the same docstring edit was made separately on three stacked branches (#2015, #2091, #2156) instead of on the bottom branch and merged up. The wrapping differed, so #2156 conflicted with #2015's live head; the coordinator caught it at release. Candidate: `merge --lane-lint <pr>` on a stacked PR refuses, or warns, when the head does not contain its base branch's current head, or when `git merge-tree` against the base conflicts. Refuse or warn: the lane decides from the false-alarm cost. Lane session_013NEJKzr9wjJhiTbhubR8Hc (coordinator 02:23 CST Nov 9). Step stack-cross-measure follows and extends this code. Lane review-record-provenance (#2440, 13:10 CST Nov 9): folded candidate lane-lint-origin-base. `merge --lane-lint <sha> --base origin/X` fetches the wrong ref, because it does not resolve origin/X to branch X, so the lint judges against the wrong base. A bare `--base X` works. Fix: resolve origin/X, or refuse it. Source: agent report, 2026-11-08 14:43 CST.
